courses.title: Government and the Breedhaven State
courses.description: Introduction to the constitutional structure of Breedhaven: the Crown, the elected Assembly, the courts, and the conventions that have shaped government since the founding of House Dawnbloom. Covers the role of the heir's education and the relationship between custom and statute.

topics.title: Crown, Assembly and Courts
topics.content: Breedhaven is a constitutional monarchy with three branches. The Crown, held by House Dawnbloom, reigns and appoints. The Assembly, 240 members elected for five-year terms, makes law and controls taxation. The courts, headed by the Court of the Charter, decide disputes and may strike down acts that breach the Charter. All three sit within a mile of one another in Seedblossom. The schoolroom summary: the Crown reigns, the Assembly rules, the courts remember.

question.ask: Which branch of government may strike down acts that breach the Charter?

topics.title: House Dawnbloom and the Charter
topics.content: House Dawnbloom united the river lordships of the lowlands and has held the throne ever since. The Charter of Seedblossom, sealed some four centuries ago, ended rule by decree: the Crown agreed to tax and legislate only through an elected Assembly, and in return the Assembly swore to the dynasty. The throne passes to the monarch's named heir, by long practice her eldest daughter. A monarch who dies with a single heir leaves no contest, only a very young queen.

question.ask: What did the Charter of Seedblossom bring to an end?

topics.title: How a Bill Becomes Law
topics.content: A bill is read three times in the Assembly. First reading is a formality, second reading debates the principle, and a committee then amends it clause by clause before third reading and the final vote. A simple majority of members present carries it, provided at least 120 of the 240 are in the chamber. The bill then goes to Dawnbloom House for royal assent. Assent has not been refused in over a century, and money bills must begin with the First Minister's government.

question.ask: How many times is a bill read in the Assembly?

topics.title: Custom, Convention and Statute
topics.content: Much of the constitution is unwritten. By convention the monarch appoints as First Minister whoever commands a majority in the Assembly, does not vote, and acts on ministers' advice. By custom the heir is educated at the University's College of Government and Law, among ordinary students. None of this is statute, and no court can enforce it. Conventions hold because breaking one costs more than keeping it. Where statute and custom conflict, statute prevails.

question.ask: Whom does the monarch by convention appoint as First Minister?
wrong: The senior justice of the courts

topics.title: Elections, Parties and the Vote
topics.content: Every citizen of eighteen or over votes, in 240 single-member districts, with the candidate who wins most votes taking the seat. Seven voters in eight are women, and about twenty sitting members are men. No seats are reserved by sex or by people. Parties form around taxation, trade and the land, but the deepest dividing line is the oldest one: Bloomist-leaning members favor policy that supports childbearing, and Freewill-leaning members resist any state hand on it.

question.ask: What do Bloomist-leaning members of the Assembly favor?

topics.title: The State and the Bloom
topics.content: No government in the Expanse can ignore the Bloom, and Breedhaven's does not try. The Ministry of Health tracks birth rates, Sire numbers and where the magical population lives. The Registry Act places fertility assays in the national Sire Registry and makes each record private, the Sire's own to disclose. Contraception is funded at every clinic. One side calls all this planning for survival. The other replies that people are not livestock, and both sit in the Assembly.

question.ask: Under the Registry Act, who may disclose a Sire's record?

skill.name: Registry grants
skill.description: You know which grants a Sire can claim: rooms and upgrades cost 15% less.

courses.title: Seminar in Governance and Reform
courses.description: Graduate seminar on contemporary challenges in Breedhaven public administration, including the management of the Sire Registry, cross-border policy in the Sown Expanse, and the capacity constraints of governing a state where seven in eight citizens are women.

topics.title: The Registry as an Administrative Problem
topics.content: Breedhaven has roughly twenty-four million people, three million of them men and some three hundred thousand of those assayed Sires. The Sire Registry holds every one of their records under the Registry Act, with each query logged against a named officer. Audits find that the central file seldom leaks. Clinics, employers and households do. The reform question is therefore not how to lock the file tighter, but whether the state can govern knowledge it does not hold.

question.ask: According to audits, where do Sire Registry leaks mostly come from?

topics.title: State Capacity at Seven to One
topics.content: Seven in eight citizens are women, so nearly the whole civil service is of childbearing age or past it. A pregnancy lasts under two months, which makes absence short but frequent, and an official's magic rises sharply while she carries. Departments plan around both: surge rosters put pregnant mages at the head of heavy circle-work, then lose them to leave within weeks. Continuity, not headcount, is the binding constraint, and no ministry has yet solved succession at short notice.

question.ask: What is the binding constraint on Breedhaven's civil service?

topics.title: Demographic Planning and its Critics
topics.content: The Ministry of Health publishes an annual Demographic Return: births, Sire numbers by province, and the distribution of magical strength. Planners use it to site schools, clinics and Bloom Chambers. Sires are unevenly spread, thick in the cities and thin in the orchard counties, and every instrument proposed to correct that is contested. Grants and housing offers are lawful. Direction of persons is not. Critics hold that even an incentive treats a man as a resource to be allocated.

question.ask: What does the Ministry of Health publish every year?

topics.title: Cross-Border Sire Policy
topics.content: Every neighbor wants strong Sires and each asks differently. Kharad-Tor negotiates openly, hold by hold, in exact contracts. Iscara's interest is clinical and run by the state. The Vesperan League folds Sire terms into trade agreements. The Starkelands are said to rest their prosperity on a single man. Breedhaven's settled doctrine is that no treaty can bind a Sire's person: the Crown may permit an arrangement, but only he can make it. Whether that doctrine survives a rich enough offer is open.

question.ask: Under Breedhaven's settled doctrine, what can no treaty bind?

topics.title: Dependence on Shared Infrastructure
topics.content: Breedhaven does not control two systems it cannot do without. Iscara built and operates the long-range portal lines, and Iscaran wards protect half the ports in the Expanse, Breedhaven's river harbors among them. A dispute with the mage state could close both within a day. Veyra's Quiet Office, the most capable intelligence service known, raises a quieter risk to Registry data. Proposed remedies, domestic ward standards and a second portal operator, are costly and decades away.

question.ask: Which state built and operates the long-range portal lines?

topics.title: Reform Under a Young Crown
topics.content: A newly crowned monarch of eighteen, still at university by custom, sharpens three reform debates. One would write the conventions on assent and the appointment of the First Minister into statute, trading flexibility for certainty. A second would make the Registrar answer to the Assembly alone, not to a minister. A third would end the custom that the heir studies among ordinary students, on security grounds. Each fixes a real weakness and removes a habit that has kept the Crown trusted.

question.ask: How old is the newly crowned monarch at the center of the reform debates?

skill.name: Knowing the scheme
skill.description: You have read the housing scheme you live under: your rent is a quarter lower.

courses.title: Foundations of Breedhaven Law
courses.description: Survey of the Breedhaven legal system: constitutional structure under House Dawnbloom, the Assembly, courts, and the hierarchy of statute and custom. Introduces legal reasoning, case analysis, and the basics of civil and criminal procedure.

topics.title: Sources of Breedhaven Law
topics.content: Breedhaven law has five sources, ranked. First is the Charter of Seedblossom, which no ordinary act may breach. Second is statute, passed by the Assembly and assented to by the Crown. Third is regulation, made by ministers under powers a statute grants. Fourth is precedent, the reasoning of earlier judgments, binding on lower courts. Fifth is custom, which a court will recognize only if it is ancient, certain and continuous. Where two sources conflict, the higher wins.

question.ask: What is the highest-ranked source of Breedhaven law?

topics.title: The Structure of the Courts
topics.content: Magistrates' courts hear minor crime and small claims in every town. The High Court tries serious crime with a jury and hears large civil suits and appeals from below. The Court of the Charter, seven justices sitting in Seedblossom, is final and alone may strike down a statute. Beside this ladder stand the Courts of Lineage, a specialist branch for paternity, inheritance and reproductive contracts, whose judges sit with a clinical assessor and hear most cases in private.

question.ask: Which court alone may strike down a statute?

topics.title: Reading and Briefing a Case
topics.content: A case brief has four parts: facts, issue, holding and reasoning. Take the teaching case Harrow v Pell. A door ward set too strong burned a courier delivering a parcel. The issue was whether a householder owes a duty of care to lawful callers. The court held that she does. Its reasoning: a ward is a thing kept on land, and its keeper must make it safe for those she invites. The holding binds later courts. Remarks made in passing do not, though they may persuade.

question.ask: In Harrow v Pell, to whom was a householder held to owe a duty of care?

topics.title: Criminal Procedure and Grave Offenses
topics.content: A person arrested must be charged or released within forty-eight hours and may have a lawyer from the first interview. Serious charges go before a High Court jury of twelve, and the Crown must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt. The defendant need prove nothing. Under the Sire Protection Act, assault, kidnapping and reproductive coercion of a Sire sit in the gravest class of offense, alongside murder, and a conviction carries a sentence measured in decades.

question.ask: Within how many hours must an arrested person be charged or released?

topics.title: Civil Procedure and Household Law
topics.content: A civil claim runs in stages: the claim, the defense, exchange of documents, trial and judgment. The claimant must prove her case on the balance of probabilities, a lower standard than in crime. Much civil work concerns households. Adults who share a home may register a household deed, which sets out shared property, liability for debts and who holds parental responsibility for each child. Leaving a household dissolves no duty to its children unless a court so orders.

question.ask: On what standard must a civil claimant prove her case?

topics.title: Persons, Privacy and Magical Liability
topics.content: Every people of the Bloom holds full legal personhood, slimes included, and a form that demands a street address cannot lawfully bar one who lives in a pond. A Sire's Registry record is private. Disclosing another person's fertility status without consent is an offense, however the knowledge was come by. Magic is judged like any other act: a caster answers for harm she could foresee. A pregnant woman's surge is foreseeable, so she must take the precautions the surge demands.

question.ask: What harm does a caster answer for under Breedhaven law?

skill.name: Claiming what is due
skill.description: You claim every allowance a father is owed: a child costs a quarter less to keep.

courses.title: Regulation and the Magitech Economy
courses.description: Advanced seminar on economic regulation in Breedhaven and the wider Sown Expanse: ward standards, Sire Registry policy, agricultural enchantment subsidies, and competition among magitech firms. Students model policy outcomes using current national data.

topics.title: Scarcity Rent in a Seven-to-One Economy
topics.content: Standard models assume labor and households come in balanced pairs; the Expanse offers neither. One birth in 80 is a fertile man, so reproductive capacity on the male side is fixed in supply and cannot be expanded by price. Whatever attaches to it earns a scarcity rent. The contested question is who captures that rent: the Sire, his household, or the state. The household of one Sire and two to five women is read by some as a pooling of that rent and by others as risk-sharing among earners.

question.ask: What fraction of births is a fertile man?

topics.title: The Sire Registry as Market Regulation
topics.content: The Registry answers an information problem: fertility cannot be observed, so without a trusted assay record false claims would flood the market in reproductive contracts and drive out honest ones. Its cost is the opposite failure: a private record still leaks, and a leak imposes on the Sire a lifelong cost he never agreed to bear. Abolitionists argue that private assay certificates would serve as well; defenders reply that only a state record stands up in the paternity and contract courts.

question.ask: What kind of market problem does the Sire Registry answer?

topics.title: Ward Standards: Safety or Barrier
topics.content: A ward standard sets minimum retention, fail-safe behavior and inspection intervals for wards sold to the public. The public-interest reading is plain: buyers cannot test a ward themselves. The capture reading notes who drafts the standards. Certification costs fall hardest on small workshops, and incumbents sit on the committees. Trade sharpens it: Iscaran wards protect half the world's ports, so a rule written to Iscaran practice imports safety and dependence together.

question.ask: On whom do ward certification costs fall hardest?

topics.title: Who Gains From Enchantment Subsidies
topics.content: Breedhaven pays growers a subsidy per charmed hectare. The stated aim is yield; the question is incidence. Growth charms are limited by labor, not land: one grower charms about half a hectare of orchard a day. With casting labor scarce, a payment per hectare is bid into the wages of casters, the fees of contract circles and orchard rents, with little effect on output. Critics propose subsidizing training instead. Defenders answer that higher rural wages for women's magic are the point.

question.ask: What are growth charms limited by?

topics.title: Monopoly and Competition in Magitech
topics.content: Magitech markets tip toward a single supplier: networks grow more valuable with each user, and enchanted infrastructure is costly to build before it carries one traveler. The long-range portal network is the limiting case: built and operated by Iscara, with no rival, and priced by treaty, not by a market. Device makers compete, but all face one bottleneck: the supply of casters to recharge what they sell. Whether to regulate portal fares as a utility or fund a second network is unresolved.

question.ask: How are fares on the long-range portal network priced?

topics.title: Sires in Trade Policy
topics.content: Access to strong Sires is negotiated between states. Kharad-Tor bargains openly for lawful access for its holds; Iscara's state takes a clinical interest; Hearthspire's prosperity is said to rest on one man of record assay; a Vesperan trade offer may carry terms concerning one Sire. Economists split three ways. One school treats such terms as trade in services, one as a claim on a person's body that no treaty can bind, and one as proof that Registry privacy cannot survive a record assay.

question.ask: Which state bargains openly for lawful access to Sires for its holds?

skill.name: Knowing the margins
skill.description: You know what things cost to stock: shops charge you a fifth less.

courses.title: Service Operations and Guest Experience
courses.description: Operational systems for hotels, banquet halls, and tourist sites, including staff scheduling, enchanted inventory tracking, and complaint resolution. Students learn to design guest experiences that accommodate diverse populations, including travelling Sires and their security needs.

topics.title: The Guest Journey and Service Design
topics.content: A stay has five stages: booking, arrival, the stay itself, departure and follow-up. A service blueprint maps each stage in two rows, what the guest sees and what the staff do out of sight to make it happen. Breedhaven hotels sell suites more than rooms, because the ordinary traveling party is a household of four to six adults. Staff never guess who shares with whom. The booking form asks only how many beds are to be made up and how many keys are wanted, and the answer is taken as given.

question.ask: How many stages does a guest's stay have?

topics.title: Rostering and Shift Design
topics.content: A roster matches staff to demand hour by hour. The working ratios are one server to eight guests for a plated dinner and one to twelve for a buffet. Magic tires, so charm duties such as warming rooms, mending linen and refreshing lights are rotated in two-hour blocks and never given to one woman for a whole shift. With pregnancies lasting under two months, leave is short but frequent, and a sound roster carries one spare in every ten. Pregnant staff are rostered away from fragile fittings.

question.ask: Why are charm duties rotated in short blocks on a roster?

topics.title: Enchanted Inventory Tracking
topics.content: Stock is tracked with tally-charms: small tags on linen, bottles and crates that register in the ledger each time they cross a warded doorway. The system sets a par level for every item. Linen par is three sets to a bed: one on it, one in the laundry and one in the store. Tally-charms fade after about ninety days and must be reset, and a tag that has faded reads as stock that has vanished. So the charmed tally is reconciled against a hand count each week, and the difference is investigated.

question.ask: What tags track hotel stock as it crosses a warded doorway?

topics.title: Hosting a Traveling Sire
topics.content: A Sire's status is his own to disclose, so it never appears in an open booking record; the reservation carries only a private-guest flag that the duty manager can read. He is roomed near a staircase, behind a logged door, with a side entrance agreed in advance with his security. Staff are briefed not to stare, not to ask and never to post his presence on Bloomr, which is cause for dismissal. Good service treats him as a guest first: his name, his breakfast order, his preference for quiet.

question.ask: What is the only mark a traveling Sire's reservation carries?

topics.title: Complaint Resolution and Service Recovery
topics.content: Complaints are handled in four steps: hear it out, apologize, mend it, follow up. The guest is never interrupted and never told the fault lies with another department. A worked case: a warming charm fails in a suite at midnight in winter. The desk apologizes, sends a heater and someone to recast within ten minutes, and rings the room an hour later. Front desk staff may refund up to one night without asking a manager. A complaint mended well leaves a guest more loyal than one who had no trouble.

question.ask: How much may front desk staff refund without asking a manager?

topics.title: Banquets, Festivals and Tourist Sites
topics.content: A banquet for two hundred is twenty tables of ten and twenty-five servers. Guests arriving by teleport array come in pulses, a dozen at once every few minutes, so the cloakroom is staffed for the pulse and not the average. Foreign parties differ: Kharadi hosts want every term written into the contract, while Vesperans expect to bargain and enjoy it. Because a birth discharges magic that can crack masonry, large venues post the route to the nearest Bloom Chamber and keep a warded quiet room.

question.ask: How many servers work a banquet for two hundred?

skill.name: Service manner
skill.description: You are good with the public: every shift pays 15% more.

courses.title: Brewing and Fermentation Science
courses.description: The biochemistry and magical theory of fermentation, covering beer, cider, mead, and Bloom-infused cordials. Weekly lab practises batch brewing, yeast management, and quality control, with attention to Breedhaven's orchard-based brewing traditions.

topics.title: Fermentation: Yeast, Sugar and Bloom
topics.content: Fermentation is yeast eating sugar and giving off alcohol and carbon dioxide. Ale yeast works warm, at 18 to 22 degrees, and finishes in about a week; lager yeast works cold, at 8 to 12, and takes a month. The Bloom is already in the water and the fruit, so every brew carries a faint charge before a brewer touches it. A coaxing charm, the same one used on houseplants, can shorten a ferment by a third, but hurried yeast throws harsh flavors. The brewhouse rule: nudge, never push.

question.ask: What does yeast give off as it eats sugar?

topics.title: Orchard Cider of the Lowlands
topics.content: Breedhaven cider apples fall into four classes: sweets, sharps, bittersweets and bittersharps. A sound lowland blend is half bittersweet, a third sharp and the rest sweet. Growth-charmed orchards give bigger fruit with thinner juice, so every pressing is checked with a hydrometer: a reading of 1.050 ferments out to about 6.5 percent. By custom pressing starts after the first frost, and farmhouse cider is left to the wild yeast on the skins, which takes three months and cannot be hurried.

question.ask: By custom, when does cider pressing start?

topics.title: Mashing, Wort and the Boil
topics.content: Beer begins with the mash: crushed malted barley held in water at 65 degrees for an hour, so that its starch turns to sugar. At 62 the beer comes out dry and thin, at 68 sweet and full. A warming charm will hold a small mash within half a degree, but anything over fifty liters is run on a steam jacket and a thermostat, because magic tires and steel does not. The sweet wort is boiled for an hour with hops, early for bitterness and in the last five minutes for aroma, then chilled fast to 20.

question.ask: At what temperature is a beer mash held for an hour?

topics.title: Mead and Honey Ferments
topics.content: Honey is nearly pure sugar and poor in what yeast needs, so mead ferments slowly and stalls if neglected. One kilo of honey to three liters of water gives about 12 percent; nutrient is added in stages on days one, three and five. Honey from hives kept in charmed orchards carries more Bloom and a floral note. Mead with fruit is a melomel, with spice a metheglin, with apple juice a cyser. By old custom a new household lays down a cask at its founding and opens it at the first naming.

question.ask: What is mead made with spice called?

topics.title: Bloom-Infused Cordials and Tonics
topics.content: A cordial is a sweetened infusion, with or without alcohol, steeped with herbs and fruit gathered from Bloom-rich ground. Its effect is modest: warmth, calm, a clearer head. The charge fades once bottled, about half of it gone in three weeks, so cordials are made small and sold fresh. The label must state the effect and its strength. Because pregnancy multiplies magic, a pregnant brewer charms at a tenth of her usual effort, and cordials made for pregnant drinkers are always alcohol-free.

question.ask: How much of a bottled cordial's charge is gone in three weeks?

topics.title: Yeast Management and Quality Control
topics.content: Healthy yeast is harvested from the bottom of one batch and pitched into the next, for five or six generations before it tires. Every batch has a log: gravity, temperature and acidity, which for beer should settle between pH 4.2 and 4.6. Common faults are named by smell: butter for diacetyl, green apple for acetaldehyde, vinegar for acetic spoilage. An unevenly cast charm leaves a batch fermenting in layers. The triangle test sets out three glasses, two alike, to find the odd one out.

question.ask: Which brewing fault smells of butter?

skill.name: Bloom cordial
skill.description: Once a week you can brew a cordial to share with a woman. For a day, whatever she takes against the Bloom does not count.

courses.title: Enchanted Cuisine and Menu Design
courses.description: Advanced cookery integrating culinary technique with deliberate magical effect, including Bloom-resonant dishes for seasonal festivals and restorative meals for pregnant women. Weekly lab develops tasting menus that balance flavour, nutrition, and magical coherence.

topics.title: Magical Coherence on the Plate
topics.content: An enchanted dish carries one intended effect, and its flavor should point the same way. Kitchen effects fall into three families: warming, soothing and quickening. A warming charm belongs in a broth with ginger and pepper, not in a chilled custard. Two opposed charms on one plate cancel and leave a flat, metallic aftertaste that any diner can detect. Coherence is the test of the craft: the charm, the seasoning and the temperature of a dish must all agree on what it is meant to do.

question.ask: What aftertaste do two opposed charms on one plate leave?

topics.title: Charmed Ingredients and Their Handling
topics.content: Growth-charmed produce reaches the kitchen already carrying a charge, strongest on the day it is picked and mostly gone within a week. Fat carries a charm, acid sharpens it and salt fixes it, which is why charmed butter keeps its effect longer than charmed lettuce. Hard boiling strips most charges, so charged herbs go in at the end, off the heat. Stock is held in a larder under a preservation charm at about four degrees, and charged and plain ingredients are shelved apart and labeled.

question.ask: When do charged herbs go into a dish?
question.answer: At the end, off the heat
wrong: At the start, with the stock

topics.title: Casting at the Stove
topics.content: There are three ways to put a charm into food. Steeping lets a charged ingredient give up its effect slowly, as in a stock or a tea. Folding works the charm in by hand during a rest, as when dough is proving. Finishing is cast over the plated dish in the last seconds before it leaves the pass. Kitchen charms are Tier I work, small and repeatable. A cook can finish about forty plates in a service before she tires, so a banquet is finished by a circle of three taking turns.

question.ask: Which way of charming food is cast over the plated dish?

topics.title: Restorative Cookery for Pregnant Women
topics.content: A pregnancy runs under two months, so the body builds fast and the appetite is enormous. Restorative menus are dense in iron, calcium and protein: liver, dark greens, eggs, bone broth, oily river fish. The diner's own rising magic amplifies any charm she eats, so dishes for pregnant women are charmed at a quarter of the usual strength, and quickening dishes are left off the menu altogether in the final weeks. Soothing dishes suit best, served warm, little and often, six small meals in a day.

question.ask: At what strength are dishes for pregnant women charmed?

topics.title: Festival Dishes of the Bloom Year
topics.content: Breedhaven's festival tables follow the orchard. At First Blossom in spring the centerpiece is the seven-and-one loaf, seven plaited strands of enriched dough around a single seeded heart, torn and shared, never cut. Pressing suppers in autumn are built on new cider, roast pork and baked apples. Bloom-resonant dishes use ingredients picked that day from charmed ground and are given only a light warming finish, since the produce already carries the season's charge and a heavy hand muddies it.

question.ask: What loaf is the centerpiece of the table at First Blossom?

topics.title: Designing the Tasting Menu
topics.content: A formal tasting menu runs to seven courses, and its effects are planned as an arc: one quickening course to open, soothing dishes through the middle, a warming close. No more than three courses are charmed, with plain dishes between to rest the palate. Every effect is printed on the menu, and an uncharmed version of each course is kept ready for guests who are pregnant or would rather not. Paired drinks must not double an effect: a warming cordial never accompanies a warming dish.

question.ask: How many courses does a formal tasting menu run to?

skill.name: Charmed confection
skill.description: Once a week you can make a confection that any woman loves to be given.

courses.title: Introduction to Bloomology
courses.description: Foundational study of the Primordial Bloom as a natural force: its presence in soil, water, and blood, its observed effects on living things, and the basic principles by which women channel it. Weekly lab introduces measurement of Bloom fields and basic exercises in directed enchantment.

topics.title: The Bloom as a Natural Force
topics.content: The Primordial Bloom is a living force present in soil, water and blood, and it is studied like any other part of nature: by observation, measurement and repeatable test. Its four standing rules open every textbook. Seven girls are born for each boy. Only women can work magic. About one man in ten is fertile. Pregnancy amplifies a woman's power. Bloomology asks how these rules operate, and leaves the question of why to the theologians.

question.ask: How many girls are born for each boy?

topics.title: Soil and Water: Ambient Fields
topics.content: Bloom field strength is measured in thaums. Ordinary tilled soil reads about two to four thaums, old orchard ground six or more, and still shaded water higher again, which is why slimes arise in ponds and not on hillsides. Fields pool where life is dense and undisturbed, and thin over bare rock and fresh concrete. A simple demonstration: two trays of cress, one on orchard loam and one on washed sand, show a visible difference in growth inside a week.

question.ask: In what unit is Bloom field strength measured?

topics.title: Blood: The Bloom in the Body
topics.content: Every living body carries the Bloom, but only a woman's can direct it. A resting adult woman reads roughly ten to twenty thaums at the wrist, varying with health, sleep and season of life. A man's blood reads much the same, and yet nothing he does will move it: he is a vessel without a channel. The difference is not one of quantity. This single observation, repeatable at any bench, overturned the old belief that men simply had less of the Bloom in them.

question.ask: What can a woman's body do with the Bloom that a man's cannot?

topics.title: Channeling: Intent, Focus and Fatigue
topics.content: A working has three parts. Intent is the clear picture of the result. Focus is the place where the result is asked for: a hand, a seam, a seedling. Release is letting the field move without forcing it. Most women manage warming, mending, a light or easing pain with no training. Magic is tiring because the body's own field is spent and must refill, usually within hours. Spell-work is graded in tiers by the output it needs, and a beginner works at Tier I.

question.ask: What are the three parts of a working?

topics.title: Measuring a Bloom Field
topics.content: The standard bench instrument is the thaumometer, a sealed glass cell of charmed water whose glow is read by a light sensor and shown as a number. Three habits make a reading trustworthy. Zero the cell away from people and plants. Take three readings and report the middle one. Note who is in the room, because a pregnant woman two benches away can lift every reading on the floor. The first exercise is a map of the teaching garden, one reading per square meter.

question.ask: What is the standard bench instrument for reading a Bloom field?

topics.title: Circles and Amplification
topics.content: One woman's field is limited, so larger workings are done in a circle. Fields in a circle do not simply add: four women working well together commonly reach five or six times the output of one, and working badly together less than two. One member leads and shapes the working while the rest feed it. The other great amplifier is pregnancy, which raises a woman's output through the whole term. The most demanding circles in industry and medicine are led by pregnant mages.

question.ask: How many times one woman's output do four working well in a circle reach?

skill.name: Resonance token
skill.description: Once a week you can charge a token. Set off beside a woman you are with, it has her need 10 less desire for a day.

courses.title: Seminar in Bloom Theology
courses.description: Graduate seminar on contemporary theological debates: the nature of the Bloom's want, post-menopausal magic, and the ethics of magical augmentation through pregnancy. Students engage with current scholarship and produce an original paper.

topics.title: The Bloom's Want: Immanence Reconsidered
topics.content: Orthodox doctrine holds the Bloom to be immanent: present in soil, water and blood, and not a deity standing outside the world. The live dispute is whether an immanent force can properly be said to want anything. The Volitional school reads the generative pull as real intention. The Tropist school, following the Order theologian Hesta Marrowgate, treats it as a leaning, as a root leans to water, and warns that speaking of want smuggles a person into a process.

question.ask: Which school treats the Bloom's pull as a leaning, not a want?

topics.title: Instinct, Not Command: The Leaning Doctrine
topics.content: The Order teaches that the Bloom inclines and never compels: a woman feels the pull and still chooses. Bloomist theologians conclude that a freely given yes to the pull is the highest act of devotion. Freewill theologians answer that consent means something only where refusal is equally honorable. The standing test case is the priestess who chooses never to bear. On the first reading she is a failed devotee. On the second she is the proof that the doctrine is true.

question.ask: Who is the standing test case of the leaning doctrine?
question.answer: The priestess who chooses never to bear
wrong: The Sire who refuses every household
The mother who conceives for power
The widow who keeps her magic

topics.title: Dampers and the Charge of Impiety
topics.content: Suppressants turn the pull down to a background hum, and theology has never agreed what that does to devotion. Rigorist Bloomists call the damper a stopped ear, a refusal to hear what is sacred. Accommodationists within the Order reply that a damper silences nothing, since the magic remains untouched, and that a quieter pull allows a clearer answer. The Order has issued no binding ruling, and most priestesses counsel by the case and not by the rule.

question.ask: What do Rigorist Bloomists call the damper?

topics.title: Second Bloom and Persisting Magic
topics.content: After menopause the pull ceases, yet a woman's magic does not leave her. This is the hardest fact for any theology that ties magic to generativity. Three answers are current. The Residue view holds that power once given is not withdrawn. The Widening view holds that generativity turns from bearing to tending, teaching and guarding. The Severance view, favored by Freewill writers, holds that magic and pull were always two separate gifts that merely travel together.

question.ask: Which view holds that magic and the pull were always two separate gifts?

topics.title: Conceiving for Power: Augmentation Ethics
topics.content: Pregnancy multiplies a woman's magic, so a child may be conceived partly for the strength it lends. Iscara assigns its greatest workings to pregnant mages as a matter of state practice. Critics call this instrumental conception and argue that it treats the child as a tool. Defenders note that no mother's motives are ever unmixed and that the surge is the Bloom's own design. The contested ground is whether an employer or a state may ever ask for it.

question.ask: Which state assigns its greatest workings to pregnant mages?

topics.title: The Theodicy of Scarcity
topics.content: If the Bloom leans toward generation, the rarity of fertile men needs explaining: seven daughters to a son, and only one son in ten a Sire. The Trial reading holds that scarcity teaches care and cooperation, and points to the household as its fruit. The Balance reading holds that an abundance of seed would exhaust the Bloom itself. A newer and sharper line asks what the Bloom owes the nine men in ten it passes over, and finds the tradition has almost nothing to say.

question.ask: What share of sons is a Sire?

skill.name: Speaking her creed
skill.description: You can talk to a devout or reluctant woman in her own terms: she needs 15 less desire.

courses.title: Practical Witchcraft: Charm, Hex and Counter
courses.description: The working witch's craft as it is practised, not theorised: small charms cast by hand, the hexes every student is warned about and how each is undone, and the discipline of working with the Bloom rather than drawing on it. Half of every week is at the bench.

topics.title: Working With, Not Drawing On
topics.content: Witchcraft is the craft of small workings done by hand, and its first discipline is to work with the Bloom and not draw on it. Drawing means spending the body's own field, which is quick and tiring. Working with means borrowing the field already present in the thing itself: the warmth left in a hearthstone, the growth in a stem. A witch who draws can light ten candles and must then sit down. One who works with the wax and the wick lights fifty.

question.ask: What does a witch spend when she draws on the Bloom?

topics.title: The Three Hand Charms
topics.content: Three charms are the grammar of the craft. Warming: cup the object, breathe once, and ask the heat already in it to gather. Mending: bring the broken edges together and hold until they remember being whole, which works on cloth, clay and wood but never on anything alive. Light: pinch the air above a surface that has seen daylight. Each holds for about an hour unless anchored to a knot, a stitch or a scratched mark, which can carry it for days.

question.ask: What will a mending charm never work on?

topics.title: Anchors, Knots and Thresholds
topics.content: A charm lasts as long as its anchor. Knots hold best in natural fiber, with nine turns as the working standard. Scratched marks hold in stone and fired clay, poorly in metal and not at all in plastic. Thresholds are natural anchors: doorsills, window frames, lids and hems all divide an inside from an outside, which is why wards sit there. A sound bench exercise is a jar ward that keeps bread fresh for a week, anchored on the thread of the lid.

question.ask: How many turns is the working standard for an anchoring knot?

topics.title: Four Hexes Worth Recognizing
topics.content: A hex is a charm set against its subject's interest. Four are common enough to meet in any residence hall. The Tangle knots hair, laces and cables. The Souring turns milk and spoils a brew. The Misplace makes one object persistently overlooked. The Stumble catches a foot on flat ground. All four are Tier I, all need an anchor near the victim, and all leave a signature: a faint cold spot that a trained hand can feel from a few inches away.

question.ask: Which hex makes one object persistently overlooked?

topics.title: Undoing: Unpick, Break, Return
topics.content: Every hex has three counters. Unpicking finds the anchor and reverses it turn by turn: slow, clean and safe. Breaking destroys the anchor by burning the knot or washing the mark in running water: fast, but the released charge goes somewhere, often into the nearest glass. Returning sends the hex back along its thread to the caster, and is forbidden at the bench because it escalates. The rule of the craft is to unpick where possible and break only when in haste.

question.ask: Which way of countering a hex is forbidden at the bench?

topics.title: Hexing, Consent and the Law
topics.content: Breedhaven law treats a hex as it treats a blow. A working set on a person or their property without consent is an offense, however small, and intent to harm is presumed where the anchor was hidden. Three cases are tried far more severely: a working on a pregnant woman, a working that interferes with contraception, and a working aimed at a Sire. The craft's own older rule is shorter. Nothing is cast on a person that could not be cast in front of them.

question.ask: What does Breedhaven law treat a hex like?

skill.name: Heartsease draught
skill.description: Once a week you can brew a draught at the bench. Drunk, it doubles the affection you win for a day.

courses.title: Introduction to Magical Engineering
courses.description: Foundations of engineering with the Bloom, covering the principles by which enchantments are structured into materials, circuits, and devices, and the safety standards that govern magical engineering in Breedhaven. Weekly lab in the Foundry introduces basic enchantment construction, measurement, and calibration.

topics.title: What Engineering Does With Magic
topics.content: Magic is personal, limited and tiring; technology is scalable and predictable. Magical engineering exists to move a working out of the woman and into a device, so that it runs when she has gone home. Every enchantment has three parts: an anchor (the material that holds it), a pattern (what it does) and a charge (the Bloom stored to drive it). A mage can heat a room for an hour. A warming charm anchored in a radiator plate and topped up monthly heats it all winter.

question.ask: What are the three parts of every enchantment?

topics.title: Anchors: Materials That Hold a Working
topics.content: An anchor is judged by retention, the share of charge still held after a set time. Living and once-living materials take a charge easily and lose it fast: untreated oak holds a ward for days. Dense crystalline materials are harder to charge and far better at keeping it: quartz, granite and fired ceramic hold for years. Copper and silver conduct a working instead of storing it, which is why they form the traces between anchors. Self-mending stone is granite carrying a mending pattern.

question.ask: What do copper and silver do with a working?

topics.title: Measuring the Bloom: Thaums and Tiers
topics.content: Charge is measured in thaums and output in thaums per hour, read on a thaumometer, a quartz sensor whose response rises with the Bloom passing through it. Tiers grade workings by the output they demand and the harm they do if they slip. Tier I covers what most women manage unaided: a light, a warming, a simple mend. Tier III and above need training, a circle or a pregnancy surge. Calibration comes first: zero the meter in a warded box, then check it against a reference stone of known charge.

question.ask: Which tier covers what most women manage unaided?

topics.title: Coupling Enchantment to Circuits
topics.content: A magitech device joins an enchantment to ordinary electronics at a coupler, a quartz element that turns a change in charge into a voltage and back. A door ward shows the pattern. The ward lives in the frame; a coupler reports its state to a microcontroller; the controller checks a phone key and tells the ward to admit or refuse. The electronics decide, the enchantment acts. The design rule follows: logic belongs in silicon, where it is cheap and testable, and force belongs in the working.

question.ask: What element joins an enchantment to ordinary electronics in a magitech device?

topics.title: Decay, Recharge and Maintenance
topics.content: Every stored charge leaks. Loss is exponential, so anchors are rated by half-life: a household ward plate at about six months, an enchanted street lamp at a year. A device is serviced before it falls below its working threshold. Recharging is skilled labor, done by hand or, for large installations, by a circle. Short-range teleport arrays are the costliest case: a station array is topped up by a circle every night, which is why arrays stand only at major stations and on the campus shuttle.

question.ask: What is the half-life of a household ward plate?

topics.title: Safety Standards and the Warded Bench
topics.content: Breedhaven law treats an enchanted device like any other product: it must fail safe, meaning a drained or broken working leaves the device inert, never active. In the Foundry every casting above Tier I is done at a warded bench, which contains a slipped working, and Tier III work needs a spotter. Pregnancy changes the arithmetic, since output climbs week by week: a pregnant engineer is re-measured weekly, moved to the advanced practical for the length of the surge, and works with a spotter.

question.ask: Where is every Foundry casting above Tier I done?

skill.name: Stamina band
skill.description: Every four days you can charge a wristband you built. Triggered, it gives you 40 energy.

courses.title: Agricultural Systems and the Bloom
courses.description: Introduction to modern agriculture in Breedhaven, covering soil science, riverine irrigation, and the role of the Bloom in crop growth and soil health. Weekly lab involves field sampling, soil Bloom measurement, and basic crop assessment at the university's experimental orchards.

topics.title: The Lowland Farm System
topics.content: Breedhaven feeds itself from three kinds of land. River bottoms carry grain and vegetables on deep silt, renewed by controlled spring flooding. The slopes above them carry orchards, the country's signature crop and its main farm export. The uplands are grazed. A typical lowland holding is mixed: forty to eighty hectares, with orchard on the best-drained ground. Nearly all holdings are worked by a household of women, and labor, not land, is the limiting factor.

question.ask: What do the slopes above the river bottoms carry?

topics.title: Soil: Texture, Structure and Life
topics.content: Soil is described by texture, the proportions of sand, silt and clay, and by structure, how those particles clump into crumbs. Texture is fixed; structure is made or ruined by management. A handful of good loam holds together when squeezed and breaks when prodded. Organic matter feeds the organisms that build structure, and a field at five percent organic matter holds markedly more water than one at two. The spade test, one clean cube lifted and read layer by layer, comes before any instrument.

question.ask: Which property of a soil is fixed and cannot be changed by management?

topics.title: Water: Rivers, Ditches and Drains
topics.content: Lowland farming is water management. The rivers are leveed, and sluice gates admit a measured flood each spring to lay silt on the bottoms. Through the growing season, gravity ditches carry water along the contour to furrows. Too much water kills as surely as too little, so tile drains under orchard ground keep roots out of standing water. An apple tree tolerates about two days waterlogged in summer. The water boards that hold the sluice keys are among the oldest elected bodies in the country.

question.ask: About how long can an apple tree tolerate waterlogged ground in summer?

topics.title: Measuring the Bloom in a Field
topics.content: The Bloom is present in soil as in everything living, and field strength is measured with a thaumometer pushed to root depth. Tilled ground reads two to four thaums and old orchard ground six or more, because long-lived roots and undisturbed soil life hold it. Readings are taken on a grid, twenty to the hectare, at the same hour, since strength rises a little after dawn. A map of the readings shows where a crop will respond to a charm and where the ground has nothing to give.

question.ask: Which instrument is pushed to root depth to measure the Bloom in a field?

topics.title: What a Crop Needs, and When
topics.content: A crop needs light, water, warmth and about a dozen nutrients, and its yield is set by whichever is shortest. Demand is not level through the season. Wheat takes most of its nitrogen in the six weeks of stem extension; an apple tree draws hardest from petal fall to midsummer, when it is building fruit and next year's buds at once. Feeding outside those windows is wasted or washed into the ditches. Matching supply to the demand curve is the core skill of the grower, with or without magic.

question.ask: A crop's yield is set by which of its needs?

topics.title: Reading a Crop in the Field
topics.content: Assessment begins with walking the field in a W, stopping at ten points, so that the edges do not mislead. At each stop the grower counts plants in a measured length of row, notes leaf color against a standard card, and looks under leaves for pests. Yellowing on old leaves first points to nitrogen; on young leaves, to iron or sulfur. In orchards the count is fruitlets per cluster after the natural drop. Every figure goes in the field book with its date: one visit shows a state, a series shows a trend.

question.ask: In what pattern does a grower walk a field to assess a crop?

skill.name: Kitchen garden
skill.description: You keep the house in fresh food: its comfort is 2 higher.

courses.title: Foundations of Sire Genetics
courses.description: Introduction to the genetics of the sex ratio and Sire fertility, covering the Bloom's role in sex determination, the clinical assay that establishes Sire status, and the basic biology of inheritance in the Sown Expanse. Weekly lab involves microscopy, assay demonstration, and basic genetic analysis.

topics.title: What Makes a Sire
topics.content: A Sire is a man whose seed can begin a pregnancy. A True Sire is the rare Sire with whom a woman who is taking nothing against it always conceives. About one man in ten is one, and men are one birth in eight, so a Sire is roughly one birth in eighty. The other nine men in ten are healthy in every ordinary sense: the difference lies in the seed alone and cannot be seen or felt by the man himself. Sire Genetics asks two questions. Why are sons so few, and why are so few sons fertile? Neither has a complete answer yet.

question.ask: About what share of men are Sires?

topics.title: Sex Determination and the Daughter Bias
topics.content: A father's seed carries the factor that decides a child's sex, in equal numbers for daughters and sons. The seven to one ratio arises afterward. The egg's own Bloom field strongly favors daughter-bearing seed, so seven conceptions in eight are girls. The proof is that the ratio holds in assisted conception, where seed and egg meet in a dish. The bias is the same in humans, elves, orcs, halflings and beastkin, which points to the Bloom and not to any one bloodline.

question.ask: What causes seven conceptions in eight to be girls?

topics.title: The Clinical Assay
topics.content: Fertility is established by assay of a seed sample. Under the microscope, fertile seed takes up a Bloom-reactive stain and glows green: this is bound seed. The result is the bound fraction, the percentage of seed that is bound. Below five percent a man is recorded as not fertile. Most Sires score between twenty and forty, and a score above ninety is a record assay and makes the news abroad. Two samples two weeks apart are required before any entry is made.

question.ask: What color does fertile seed glow under the assay's stain?

topics.title: Does Fertility Run in Families?
topics.content: Only weakly. The sons of Sires are fertile about one time in six, against one in ten for men at large, and the brothers of a Sire fare little better than strangers. So fertility is not a single inherited trait passed from father to son. The working model is that many small inherited factors raise or lower the chance, and that the mother's Bloom field during the pregnancy matters as much. Assay scores among fertile kin do show a clear family resemblance.

question.ask: About how often are the sons of Sires fertile themselves?

topics.title: Registry Data and Its Limits
topics.content: Every assay result is entered in the national Sire Registry, and the record is private by law. Geneticists never see names. Research uses stripped records: score, age, people and region, released under license. Two cautions apply to any Registry study. Men who are never assayed do not appear, so the one in ten figure is an estimate. And a count of three Sires in one small town cannot be published at all, because a number that small identifies the men.

question.ask: What do geneticists never see in the Registry records released for research?

topics.title: Why So Few: Open Questions
topics.content: Three hypotheses compete. The Cost hypothesis holds that binding seed draws heavily on the Bloom, so that only a few bodies can sustain it. The Maternal Field hypothesis places the cause in the womb, where a mother's field sets her son's fertility before birth. The Balance hypothesis treats scarcity as a stable ratio the Bloom returns to whenever it is disturbed. No treatment has ever made an infertile man fertile, and any model must explain that failure.

question.ask: Which hypothesis places the cause of Sire scarcity in the womb?

skill.name: Knowing your own assay
skill.description: You understand what you are. The chance of a child with a woman on birth control is half as high again.

courses.title: Clinical Midwifery
courses.description: The working practice of the profession Breedhaven depends on most: antenatal care across a seven-week term, attending a birth in a Bloom Chamber, and the care of mother and child in the days after. Taught on the ward at the Reproductive Health Center, with supervised shifts.

topics.title: The Seven-Week Term
topics.content: A pregnancy runs forty-eight days from conception to birth, and the midwife's calendar is built on it. The first visit is in the first week, to confirm the Bloom has locked in and to take a baseline of the mother's field strength. Visits are then weekly, and twice weekly from the fifth week. Each records weight, pulse, the child's movement and the mother's reading on the thaumometer. A term this short leaves no slack: a problem found on a Solday has to be acted on by Windsday.

question.ask: How many days does a pregnancy run from conception to birth?

topics.title: Reading the Surge
topics.content: A mother's magic rises through her term and the curve is diagnostic. A small lift is expected in the early weeks, a marked one in the middle, and a steep climb near term. A reading that stalls or falls for two visits running is the earliest sign that something is wrong with the pregnancy, often before any physical symptom. A reading that climbs too fast calls for warded rest, because a mother who cannot hold her own working is a danger to herself. The chart is plotted at every visit, by hand.

question.ask: What is the earliest sign that something is wrong with a pregnancy?
question.answer: A stalled or falling magic reading

topics.title: The Bloom Chamber
topics.content: Births take place in a Bloom Chamber: a warded room built to contain the peak of a mother's magic, which arrives with labor. The wards are set to her own baseline and checked that morning. Nothing enchanted is brought in, including phones. A second practitioner stands by as spotter with a grounding rod, whose only job is to bleed off a surge. The mother casts nothing deliberately. Most births need no intervention beyond this, and the chamber is why home birth is rare outside the country districts.

question.ask: What does the spotter at a birth use to bleed off a surge?

topics.title: Labor and Its Stages
topics.content: Labor is shorter than the old texts from abroad describe, commonly four to eight hours from the first regular pains. The first stage ends when the mother's field peaks and steadies, which a practiced midwife feels before any instrument shows it. The second stage, delivery, rarely lasts an hour. The third is the afterbirth, and with it the mother's magic falls back sharply over a few minutes, which can leave her faint. She is kept lying down and warm until her reading has settled near baseline.

question.ask: How long does labor commonly last from the first regular pains?

topics.title: The Lying-In Week
topics.content: The seven days after a birth are the lying-in week. The mother's magic is at its lowest and she tires easily. She is visited daily for the first three days and again on the seventh. The checks are bleeding, fever, feeding and mood, in that order of urgency. The Bloom will not lock in again until she has recovered, and a midwife says so plainly to any household in a hurry. A mother well fed, rested and unworried recovers faster, and that is the practical case for a household sharing the work.

question.ask: Which lying-in check comes first in order of urgency?

topics.title: Fathers, Households and the Birth
topics.content: A father in the room changes outcomes, and the profession's own figures say so: labors with him present are shorter on average and the mother's field steadier. Since a Sire may have several partners near term at once, clinics give each mother a set hour and ask him to keep it. The midwife's duty is to the mother alone. She records who attended, never why someone did not, and she keeps a household's quarrels out of the chamber by asking everyone but the father and one companion to wait outside.

question.ask: To whom is the midwife's duty owed?

skill.name: Lying-in care
skill.description: You know how a mother is looked after: she can conceive again in half the time after a birth.

courses.title: Foundations of Strength Training
courses.description: Introduction to resistance training, conditioning, and movement mechanics for students of all body types and Bloom states. Weekly lab covers proper lifting technique, programme design, and safe training practices for pregnant and non-pregnant students alike.

topics.title: Six Movements and the Brace
topics.content: All strength training is built from six movements: squat, hinge, push, pull, lunge and carry. Before any of them comes the brace. The lifter breathes low into the belly, tightens the trunk as if about to take a punch, and holds the spine in its natural curve from start to finish. A broomstick laid along the back should touch the head, the upper back and the tailbone throughout a hinge. If one of the three points lifts off, the back has moved, and no weight is added until it stays put.

question.ask: What must a lifter master before any of the six movements?

topics.title: The Squat and the Deadlift
topics.content: In the squat the bar sits across the upper back, feet are set shoulder width with toes turned slightly out, and the hips drop until they are just below the top of the knee. Knees track over the toes and the heels stay down. In the deadlift the bar starts over the middle of the foot, the hips hinge back, the arms hang straight, and the legs push the floor away. In both lifts the bar travels in a straight vertical line over mid-foot. A beginner learns both with an empty twenty-kilo bar.

question.ask: In the squat and the deadlift, the bar travels over which part of the foot?

topics.title: Pressing, Rowing and Balance
topics.content: The bench press and the overhead press train pushing; the row and the pull-up train pulling. On the bench, the shoulder blades are pinched together, the feet stay planted, and the bar touches the lower chest. Overhead, the bar finishes above the ears with the elbows locked. A sound program does at least as many pulling sets as pushing sets, since desks and phones already round the shoulders forward. One spotter stands at the head of the bench for any set taken near its limit.

question.ask: How many pulling sets should a sound program include, compared with pushing sets?

topics.title: Program Design and Progressive Overload
topics.content: A muscle grows stronger only when asked for slightly more than last time; this is progressive overload. The beginner's plan is three sessions a week with a rest day between, three sets of five on each main lift. Each session adds 2.5 kilos to the bar. A worked example: a squat begun at 40 kilos reaches 70 after twelve sessions, four weeks. When a weight fails twice running, it is cut by a tenth and built back up. Sleep, food and rest days are part of the plan and not a break from it.

question.ask: How much weight does the beginner's plan add to the bar each session?

topics.title: Magical Aid and the Three Divisions
topics.content: Sport is played in three divisions: Unaugmented, with no magic; Mage, which allows it; and Bloom, for pregnant competitors. A strengthening nudge will move more weight on the day, but tendons and bone adapt only to load they actually bear, so an augmented lifter with no plain base gets hurt. The rule in the weight room is no pain-easing charm before or during a session, because pain is the warning. A healer can close a strain in minutes, but the mended tissue still needs its rest days.

question.ask: Which kind of charm is banned before or during a session in the weight room?

topics.title: Training Through Pregnancy
topics.content: A pregnant lifter is hardier than before and her power rises week by week, but in a pregnancy of under two months her balance and her joints change faster than her habits. Training goes by effort, not by numbers: every set stops with two clean repetitions in hand. Breath is never held under load, and after the middle weeks nothing is pressed lying flat. Maximum attempts are made only on a warded platform with a spotter, since a surge under the bar can bend steel.

question.ask: A pregnant lifter's training goes by what, instead of by numbers?

skill.name: Programme design
skill.description: You train properly: work on strength and endurance goes half as far again.

courses.title: Athletic Performance and Coaching
courses.description: The senior course in sport: how a season is planned, how a squad is led, and how magic is and is not allowed on the field. Half of every week is at the Tiltyard, coaching a junior side under supervision.

topics.title: Planning a Season Backward
topics.content: A season is planned from its last match backward. The Arena Finals fall in the closing weeks of term, so a squad should peak then and not in the opening fixtures. The year is cut into blocks of three to five weeks: a base block of high volume and low intensity, a build block where volume falls and intensity climbs, and a taper of seven to ten days before the match that matters. A coach who trains hardest in the final week sends tired players onto the field.

question.ask: From which point is a season planned?

topics.title: Load, Fatigue and the Training Log
topics.content: Training load is volume multiplied by intensity, and it is written down. The simplest measure is session minutes times a rating of effort from one to ten, totalled by week. A jump of more than a tenth from one week to the next is where most soft-tissue injuries come from. Fatigue shows first in sleep, mood and resting pulse, a day or two before it shows in performance. The log exists so that a coach can see the bad week coming instead of explaining it afterward.

question.ask: How is training load calculated?

topics.title: Magic on the Field: The Three Divisions
topics.content: University sport is played in three divisions, set by how much magic is allowed. The Open division permits any working a player can cast unaided. The Limited division allows only Tier I workings and bans anything cast on an opponent. The Plain division allows none, and wards on the pitch void a match if one is tripped. Men play almost entirely in the Plain division. Most of the crowd follows Limited, where skill and a small working decide a point together.

question.ask: Which workings does the Limited division allow?

topics.title: Pregnant Athletes and the Surge Rule
topics.content: A pregnant player's magic climbs steeply through her term, which upsets any division that allows casting. The surge rule answers it: from the middle weeks she is reclassified upward, playing Open even if she registered for Limited, and she takes the field only with a warded spotter on the touchline. Physical load is cut by a third, contact drills stop, and she is not asked to play through a term's last fortnight. No coach may bench a player for being pregnant; the rule changes where she plays, not whether.

question.ask: By how much is a pregnant athlete's physical load cut under the surge rule?

topics.title: Leading a Squad of Twelve
topics.content: A captain leads by what she tolerates. The first job is standards: who is on time, who finishes the last rep, who speaks to an official. The second is the bench, because a squad of twelve fields six or seven and the rest decide the mood. A workable rule is to give every player a named role and one thing she is trusted with, and to give bad news in private and credit in front of the squad. Rivalries inside a team are managed by pairing the rivals in drills, never by pretending they are friends.

question.ask: How should a captain give bad news to a member of her squad?

topics.title: Reading a Match and Changing It
topics.content: A coach watches for three things in the opening ten minutes: where the opposition's best player wants the ball, which of her own players is a step slow, and what the official is letting go. A timeout is spent to change one thing only, said in one sentence. Substitutions are for tempo as often as for tiredness: a fresh server changes the rhythm of a set. The post-match review happens the next day, with the scoresheet, and starts with what went right.

question.ask: When does the post-match review take place?

skill.name: Conditioned
skill.description: Classes and shifts take a quarter less out of you.

courses.title: Protective Operations and Sire Security
courses.description: Capstone course in executive and high-value protective operations, emphasising Sire escort detail, threat assessment, and coordination with national Sire Registry enforcement. Weekly lab runs simulated protection scenarios under graduated magical and physical pressure.

topics.title: Threat Assessment for Sire Principals
topics.content: Threats to a Sire fall into five classes: abduction, reproductive coercion, fraud, crowd pressure and disclosure. Violence is the rarest. Most incidents begin with a leak of status, then fixation by people who mean no harm and still close every exit. An assessment scores each venue for the number of young women present who have never carried a child, in whom the Bloom's pull runs strongest, and for how widely the principal's status is already known. Known status doubles the detail.

question.ask: What do most incidents involving a Sire begin with?

topics.title: Structure of a Protective Detail
topics.content: A standard escort detail is four: a leader who stays at the principal's shoulder, a close escort, an advance officer who reaches each venue first, and a driver who never leaves the vehicle. On foot the team walks a diamond with the principal at its center. Officers of childbearing age take suppressants on duty as a matter of protocol, so that attention stays on the crowd. Officers in their Second Bloom feel no pull at all and are prized for night and residential posts.

question.ask: How many officers make up a standard escort detail?

topics.title: Advance Work and Secure Venues
topics.content: The advance officer surveys a venue for three things: entrances, wards and exits by magic. Every door the principal uses should be logged, as in a university Sire wing, and one entrance reserved. Existing wards are tested, since a ward set to keep people out can as easily keep a detail in. Short-range teleport arrays at stations are the classic abduction point: a principal moved forty paces is out of sight. Details board last, hold the platform, and never split across two arrays.

question.ask: What at a station is the classic abduction point?

topics.title: Magical Threat and Counter-Warding
topics.content: The principal has no magic and every likely adversary has some. Most women manage only a nudge, a light or a minor ward, which a trained officer shrugs off. The serious cases are a circle of several casters and a pregnant adversary, whose power near term can exceed the whole detail's. Doctrine against either is distance and departure, not contest. Detail officers carry warded armor and a blade. Firearms belong to the army and city police and stay outside University walls.

question.ask: What is the doctrine against a circle of casters or a pregnant adversary?

topics.title: Registry Enforcement and Legal Limits
topics.content: Registry enforcement officers investigate unlawful disclosure, forged assays and coerced contracts, and a detail that witnesses any of these must preserve evidence and report within a day. The detail itself has no special powers. Its officers may use reasonable force to defend the principal and may detain an attacker until police arrive. They may not detain the principal. He is the client, not the cargo, and if he chooses to leave with someone, the detail advises, records and follows.

question.ask: What does a detail do if the principal chooses to leave with someone?

topics.title: Protection or Custody: Contested Cases
topics.content: The unsolved problem of Sire security is where protection becomes custody. Secure housing, logged doors and escorts reduce attempted walk-offs, yet a man who cannot go for coffee alone is not obviously safe so much as kept. Foreign offers complicate it: an approach from abroad may be a lawful contract proposal, an intelligence operation or both. Current doctrine grades restriction by assessed threat and requires the principal's written consent, renewed each term, for anything beyond escort.

question.ask: What does current doctrine require for any restriction on a Sire beyond escort?

skill.name: Reading a room for trouble
skill.description: You see a scene coming and choose your ground: you are walked in on half as often.

courses.title: Ethics of Everyday Magic
courses.description: Introduction to moral reasoning about common magical practices: household wards, Bloom suppressants, fertility assays, and enchantments embedded in consumer goods. Students examine consent, privacy, and the line between personal magic and public harm.

topics.title: Why Everyday Magic Raises Moral Questions
topics.content: Every woman has some magic and most of it is small: a warmth, a mending, a light, a ward, a nudge. Small acts done by millions of people each day are exactly what ethics is for. Three tests recur. Consent: did the person affected agree? Privacy: did the working reveal what was not offered? Harm: who bears the cost if it goes wrong? A fourth matter sits beneath all three, and every first-year writes on it. Does a will the Bloom leans on still count as free?

question.ask: Which three tests recur in the ethics of everyday magic?

topics.title: Wards, Thresholds and Neighbors
topics.content: A household ward is the commonest enchantment there is and the easiest to misuse. A ward that refuses entry is a locked door. A ward that hurts whoever tries the handle is a trap, and the courier, the meter reader and the lost child meet it first. The working rule is proportion: a ward may do no more than the keeper could rightly do in person. Shared homes add a second problem. A ward keyed by one member of a household can shut out another, and locks are a form of speech.

question.ask: Under the rule of proportion, a ward may do no more than what?
question.answer: What its keeper could rightly do in person
wrong: What the district's law sets out
What the neighbors have agreed to
What its keeper has paid a warder for

topics.title: Consent and the Kindly Nudge
topics.content: Easing a friend's headache without asking seems harmless. The difficulty is that the same act, a small working on another person's body or mood, covers calming someone who is rightly angry. The standard position is that magic worked on a person needs that person's consent, however kind the aim. Two exceptions are accepted: emergency healing where the patient cannot answer, and wards a person walks into knowingly. A glamour raises the inverse case, since it works on everyone who looks.

question.ask: What does magic worked on a person need, however kind the aim?

topics.title: Suppressants and the Authentic Self
topics.content: Dampers are cheap, legal and ordinary, and turn the Bloom's pull down to a background hum. One view holds that taking them is self-government: a person chooses the conditions under which she chooses. Another holds that muting an instinct muffles part of the self. A third view cuts across both. The clearer wrong is pressure, whether a household urging a member to stop her dampers or an employer expecting her to stay on them. Either way someone else is deciding how loud her wants are.

question.ask: What does the third view call the clearer wrong where dampers are concerned?

topics.title: The Assay and the Right Not to Tell
topics.content: A clinical assay establishes whether a man is a Sire, and the result is recorded in the national Registry. The record is private and the status is his to disclose. The ethical ground is that the fact changes how everyone treats him: a known Sire is a prospect before he is a person. So asking on a first date is rude, repeating what one was told is a serious breach, and guessing aloud is little better. The hard case is a household weighing a child, where his silence shapes others' lives.

question.ask: Who has the right to disclose that a man is a Sire?

topics.title: Enchanted Goods and Public Harm
topics.content: Enchantment is built into what people buy: growth-charmed fruit, self-mending stone, lighting, a salon tattoo that moves. A buyer cannot inspect a charm as she can a seam, so the maker's duty to say what a thing does, and for how long, is stronger than for plain goods. Public harm is the limit of private magic. A pregnant woman whose surge cracks a neighbor's wall intended nothing, yet she knew the surge was coming. Responsibility can exist without fault, and precautions follow from it.

question.ask: Why is a maker's duty to say what a thing does stronger for enchanted goods?
question.answer: A buyer cannot inspect a charm

skill.name: Good faith
skill.description: You argue honestly and it shows: trust grows a quarter faster.

courses.title: Advanced Seminar: Freewill and Bloomism
courses.description: Capstone seminar on the central debate of women's studies: whether the Bloom's wants are a woman's own. Students engage primary philosophical and political texts, produce a substantial research paper, and present to the colloquium. Prerequisite: WST 201 and one additional WST course.

topics.title: Framing the Oldest Argument
topics.content: The question is whether a want the Bloom produces belongs to the woman who feels it. Two claims must be kept apart. The causal claim, that the Bloom inclines women toward generativity and above all toward pregnancy, is agreed by all sides. The ownership claim is the dispute. Bloomists hold the want is hers and sacred. Freewill advocates hold it acts upon her without being her. The facts do not divide the two camps. What divides them is what counts as a self.

question.ask: Which claim about the Bloom is agreed by all sides of the debate?

topics.title: Classical Bloomism and its Texts
topics.content: Classical Bloomism begins from the fact that the Bloom is in the blood, not outside it. A want that rises from a woman's own living substance cannot be foreign to her, any more than hunger is. On this view resisting the pull is a kind of self-estrangement, and the Order teaches accord: to know the want, name it and act with it. The strong form calls suppressants a mutilation of the will. The moderate form, now the majority, treats them as a pause that settles nothing.

question.ask: What does the Order teach in place of resisting the pull?

topics.title: The Freewill Tradition
topics.content: Freewill writers accept the Bloom's influence and deny its title. The founding argument is from choice: the pull is an instinct, not a command, and a woman can and does refuse it. What can be refused is a proposal made to the self, not the self. The tradition's central text, Maud Hollin's The Leaning Will, gives it the image still used: the Bloom leans on a woman as wind leans on a walker, and nobody says the wind chose her road. Critics reply that a walker is not made of wind.

question.ask: Who wrote The Leaning Will?

topics.title: The Damper and the Two Selves
topics.content: Suppressants turn the pull down to a background hum, and both camps claim the result. Freewill advocates say the woman on dampers is the baseline, her judgment cleared of pressure. Bloomists say she is the altered one, since the pill is the intervention and the want is the nature. This is the two selves problem: no neutral state exists from which to ask which woman is authentic. Surveys do not settle it, because each self tends to endorse the choices made while she was in charge.

question.ask: Which problem says no neutral state exists from which to judge which woman is authentic?

topics.title: Second Bloom as a Test Case
topics.content: After menopause the pull is simply absent, which makes older women the nearest thing to a neutral witness. If most repudiated their earlier wants, the Freewill reading would gain; if most endorsed them, the Bloomist one would. The evidence is mixed and contested. Many women in their Second Bloom describe their childbearing as their own best work and also say they would not want the pull back. Whether that is endorsement, or the ordinary kindness people show their past, is disputed.

question.ask: What is absent after menopause, making older women the nearest thing to a neutral witness?

topics.title: From Philosophy to Policy
topics.content: The debate has consequences. Free suppressants at every clinic are a Freewill settlement in practice, and the Bloomist case for supporting motherhood shapes housing and leave. The Sire Registry divides both camps internally. Recent compatibilist work argues that origin is the wrong test: a want is a woman's own if she would endorse it on reflection, whatever caused it. The objection is the regress. Reflection is done by a mind the Bloom also leans on, and no vantage lies outside it.

question.ask: Which policy is a Freewill settlement in practice?

skill.name: Hearing her out
skill.description: You know how to be wrong well: losses of affection and trust are halved.

courses.title: Intermediate Language and Translation
courses.description: Continued development of reading, writing, and conversational fluency in the student's chosen language track, with introduction to translation theory and the particular challenges of rendering magical and legal terminology across Expanse cultures.

topics.title: Five Tongues of the Expanse
